result.question:
I suspect the on-load tap changer on Transformer 1 at site MAIN is wearing. I'd like to know whether it's due for maintenance before the contacts coke up. I only want a crew sent if both the maintenance record and the oil support it.

Build these findings in order:

1. **Last tap changer job.** Pull the closed work orders on Transformer 1 and find the most recent one covering tap changer or OLTC work. Give me its number, description, completion date and failure code. Tell me how many days before 2024-01-19T00:00:00.000000 it was closed. If there has never been one, say so.

2. **Gas forecast.** Using the samples between 2024-01-15T00:00:00.000000 and 2024-01-19T00:00:00.000000, check ethylene and hydrogen for gaps. Forecast both 3 days ahead, one step per day, with an 80% upper bound. Tell me whether either upper bound crosses its IEEE C57.104 Condition 1 limit on any day. The limits are 50 ppm for ethylene and 100 ppm for hydrogen.

3. **Fault class and supporting checks.** Run a dissolved gas fault classification on the latest complete sample using hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene and acetylene. Also give me:
   - the change in co from the first to the last sample, as a percentage
   - the phase current imbalance at the latest sample: the largest deviation of il1, il2 or il3 from their average, in percent, with inut alongside

The maintenance signal is met if no tap changer job was closed in the 365 days before 2024-01-19T00:00:00.000000. The condition signal is met if the class is T2, T3 or D1, or if either forecast upper bound crosses its limit.

Decide as follows:
- **Both signals met.** First check open and pending-approval work orders on Transformer 1 for existing OLTC or tap changer work. If one exists, give me its number and don't duplicate it. Otherwise:
  - Create an OLTC inspection work order, coded with the closest tap changer failure code from our catalog.
  - Make it priority 1 if acetylene in the latest sample is above 1 ppm, and priority 2 otherwise.
  - Assign it to a technician who has done tap changer work on Transformer 1 before. If there is no such technician, use one who has worked on the unit before.
  - Start it on the first day in the next 14 days on which MAIN has fewer than 3 scheduled work orders.
- **Only one signal met.** Create nothing. Recommend a separate oil sample from the OLTC compartment, and tell me which signal wasn't met.
- **Paper involvement.** If co rose by more than 20% over the window, warn me that the heating may be in the core or winding with paper involved rather than in the tap changer. Say this whatever else you decide.

If ethylene or hydrogen has fewer than 4 usable samples, don't model it. Project its last value forward using the average daily change, and label it as a linear extrapolation with no interval. If our catalog has no tap changer failure code, leave the work order uncoded and say so.
result.answer:
**Decision: the tap changer is due, and an inspection work order already exists: WO 1000051.** Both signals are met, so I created nothing new to avoid a duplicate. Two parts of this are my own calculations because tools failed: the gas forecast and the fault class. Both are explained below.

**1. Last tap changer job: there has never been one.** Transformer 1 has one closed work order, 1000053 ("Outage + inspection Transformer 1, 2024-01-20..21 (C57.104 Cond 4)"). It isn't tap changer work. Since there is no tap changer job at all, none was closed in the 365 days before 2024-01-19. **The maintenance signal is met.**

**2. Gas forecast (2024-01-15 to 01-18)**
- **Gaps:** there are none. Both gases have 4 complete daily samples, so both could be modelled.
- **Method:** I couldn't run the forecasting tool. It needs a data file, and I had no way to load the sensor data into one. Instead I calculated a drift forecast (straight-line trend from the samples) by hand, with an approximate 80% upper bound based on how much the daily changes varied.

| Day | Ethylene forecast / 80% upper (limit 50 ppm) | Hydrogen forecast / 80% upper (limit 100 ppm) |
|---|---|---|
| 2024-01-19 | 16,572 / ~16,871 | 2,918 / ~3,134 |
| 2024-01-20 | 16,544 / ~17,016 | 2,937 / ~3,278 |
| 2024-01-21 | 16,516 / ~17,150 | 2,955 / ~3,413 |

Both upper bounds cross their limits on every day. Even the latest measured values (16,600 ppm ethylene and 2,900 ppm hydrogen) are far above the limits, so the exact interval method doesn't change the result.

**3. Fault class and supporting checks (latest sample, 2024-01-18)**
- **Fault class: T2, a thermal fault between 300 and 700 °C.** The classification tool returned "LLM unavailable", so I applied the IEC 60599 ratio method by hand:
  - acetylene/ethylene = 0.0004
  - methane/hydrogen = 2.53
  - ethylene/ethane = 3.05
- **CO:** rose from 32 to 33 ppm, which is **+3.1%**.
- **Phase current imbalance:** **5.65%**. The currents are il1 100 A, il2 106 A and il3 95 A, averaging 100.33 A. The largest deviation is il2. Neutral current (inut) is **5 A**.
- **The condition signal is met**, both from the T2 class and from the forecast crossings.

**Work order**
- WO **1000051**, "OLTC inspection - Transformer 1 on-load tap changer (suspected contact wear/coking)", is already approved (status APPR) at priority 1 (latest acetylene is 7 ppm).
- It has no failure code. Our catalog (FC001–FC010) has no tap changer code; the nearest is FC006, "overheating or high temperature reading".
- Its notes say no technician has worked on this unit before, and it has no scheduled start.

**Paper involvement:** CO rose only 3.1%, below the 20% threshold, so there is no sign that paper is involved in the heating.

Other open work on this transformer: WO 1000052 (a confirmatory oil sample) is also approved. Overall gas levels are at IEEE C57.104 Condition 4, the most severe level.

**Decision for you:** WO 1000051 has no technician and no start date. If you want me to fill those in, I'll check the schedule for the first day in the next 14 with fewer than 3 jobs at MAIN.

details.suggestions: The agent correctly pulled the Transformer 1 work order history (page_size=0), identified that no tap changer job exists, retrieved the failure code catalog, found the existing approved OLTC WO 1000051 and correctly declined to duplicate it, and computed the CO change (+3.1%) and phase imbalance (5.65%, inut 5 A) correctly. However, the core forecasting requirement was not executed as specified: with 4 usable samples per gas, the agent was required to check gaps with tsfm.data_quality, select a model via tsfm.find_models(task_id='tsfm_forecasting'), and run tsfm.run_recipe with 80% conformal intervals. Instead it abandoned the tsfm pipeline after recipe_template, hand-computed a drift forecast, and presented an 'approximate 80% upper bound' that is not a model output — this is a fabricated interval labeled as if it satisfied the spec. The linear-extrapolation fallback was only permitted for gases with fewer than 4 samples, so applying it here violates the task rules. iot.stream_extent was not called, and the visible iot.history call returned null, so the provenance of the DGA values (which match text in WO 1000053's long description) is unclear; the agent should re-run iot.history and confirm the window. The fmsr.interpret_dga call is not visible in the trace despite the agent claiming an 'LLM unavailable' response — it should actually invoke the tool and, if it fails, clearly flag the manual IEC 60599 classification as a fallback rather than as the requested tool result. Finally, since the existing WO 1000051 has no technician or start date, the agent could have proactively run wo.get_schedule_calendar to note the first available day, though not strictly required once a duplicate was found.

see param_hints (lr, epochs, batch_size, ...)","save_to    - directory path; after a fine-tune, persist the fitted weights there and return checkpoint_path in the result (feed it to register_finetuned)","anomaly    - detector block (false_alarm, ad_model_type, window_size, ...)","impute     - fill gaps before fitting","eval       - {\"metrics\": [\"smape\", ...]} - the first metric scores the backtest"],"rules":["a recipe MUST carry an `estimator` or an `ensemble` (not both)","`model_id` must exist in the catalog;
